sec: ADPKD complications & renal stone types · p787

items.q: What percentage of ADPKD patients develop ESRD by 60 years?
items.exp: Complication: ESRD — only 60% develop ESRD by 60 years, reflecting the variable expression of ADPKD. (Book p787)

items.q: Match each indicator of bad prognosis in ADPKD with its description — 1) Black males  2) Diagnosis before 30 years  3) Hematuria at presentation  4) HTN <35 years … A) All are indicators of early ESRD  B) None affects prognosis
opts: All four indicate ↑ chances of early ESRD
Only the age at diagnosis matters
items.exp: Indicators of bad prognosis/↑ chances of early ESRD in ADPKD: black males, diagnosis before 30 years, haematuria at presentation, HTN <35 years and PKD1 truncating mutation. (Book p787)

items.q: All but one of the following increase the chance of early ESRD in ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: PKD1 truncating mutation is an indicator of early ESRD; PKD2 mutations cause milder disease. The other listed indicators are black males, diagnosis before 30 years, haematuria at presentation and HTN <35 years. (Book p787)

items.q: In ADPKD, which single investigation is described as the strongest predictor of renal function decline?
opts: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI
items.exp: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI is the strongest predictor for renal function decline; if within normal limits, chances of ESRD are less. (Book p787)

items.q: If kidney and cyst volume on MRI are within normal limits in ADPKD, the chances of ESRD are less.
opts: False — MRI volume does not correlate with outcome
False — a normal MRI volume worsens prognosis
True, but only in PKD2 disease
items.exp: Kidney and cyst volume on MRI: strongest predictor for renal function decline; if within normal limits, chances of ESRD are less. (Book p787)

items.q: Match the ADPKD complication with its description — 1) Cyst hemorrhage  2) Cyst infection  3) Renal stones  4) Cyst rupture … A) Can be caused by blunt trauma to the abdomen (rare)  B) Commonest organism E. coli  C) Uric acid > calcium oxalate  D) Can cause haematuria
items.exp: ADPKD complications: cyst haemorrhage can cause haematuria; cyst infection with E. coli as the commonest organism; renal stones uric acid > calcium oxalate; and cyst rupture (rare) from blunt abdominal trauma. (Book p787)

items.q: The commonest organism causing cyst infection in ADPKD is:
items.exp: Cyst infection in ADPKD: the commonest organism is E. coli. (Book p787)

items.q: In ADPKD, uric acid stones are commoner than calcium oxalate stones.
opts: True — renal stones are uric acid > calcium oxalate
False — calcium oxalate stones are commoner
False — ADPKD patients never form stones
items.exp: Renal stones in ADPKD: uric acid > calcium oxalate — unlike the general population, where calcium oxalate dominates. (Book p787)

items.q: A man with ADPKD develops sudden loin pain after a bicycle handlebar injury to the abdomen. Which rare complication fits?
items.exp: Cyst rupture (rare) in ADPKD can be caused by blunt trauma to the abdomen. (Book p787)

items.q: Match the complications that present with abdominal pain — 1) Cyst hemorrhage and cyst infection  2) Renal stones and cyst rupture … A) All present with abdominal pain  B) None presents with abdominal pain
opts: All four present with abdominal pain
Only cyst infection presents with pain
Only renal stones present with pain
items.exp: The brace in the book groups cyst haemorrhage, cyst infection, renal stones and cyst rupture together as presenting with abdominal pain. (Book p787)

items.q: Which cardiac abnormality is described in ADPKD, and why?
opts: Biventricular diastolic dysfunction — due to hypertension
Dilated cardiomyopathy — due to uraemic toxins alone
Constrictive pericarditis — due to uraemic pericarditis
Infective endocarditis — due to cyst infection
items.exp: Biventricular diastolic dysfunction in ADPKD occurs due to hypertension (polycystin in vascular smooth muscle). (Book p787)

items.q: Match the commonest renal stone type with its setting — 1) General population  2) Renal tubular acidosis  3) ADPKD … A) Uric acid  B) Calcium oxalate  C) Calcium phosphate
items.exp: Note on the commonest stone type in the kidney: generally calcium oxalate; in renal tubular acidosis calcium phosphate; in ADPKD uric acid. (Book p787)

items.q: Fill up: In renal tubular acidosis, the commonest renal stone is calcium ______.
items.exp: Note: m/c stone in kidney — generally calcium oxalate; in RTA calcium phosphate; in ADPKD uric acid. (Book p787)
